mcat_description.short: A prefabricated guest house is a factory-manufactured, modular accommodation structure assembled on-site from pre-built components — typically an MS or steel frame with insulated sandwich panel walls and roof — designed for temporary or semi-permanent residential use at industrial, institutional, or hospitality sites.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated guest houses are off-site manufactured modular structures built using mild steel (MS) or light gauge steel frames combined with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool core) for walls and roofing, enabling rapid on-site assembly without conventional masonry. They are sold as complete turnkey units or in customisable configurations ranging from single-room porta cabin modules to multi-room complexes with attached toilets, electrical fittings, and plumbing. In the Indian B2B market, the dominant commercial form is the MS porta cabin-style guest house used at construction sites, industrial campuses, mining projects, defence establishments, and institutional premises requiring temporary or relocatable accommodation. Structural components are engineered as per IS standards, and units are designed for easy disassembly, relocation, and reuse across project sites.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, prefabricated guest houses are commercially dominated by MS (mild steel) frame structures with insulated sandwich panel walls and roofing — commonly called 'porta cabins' or 'prefab cabins' — manufactured by a large base of SME fabricators concentrated in Delhi NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu. Structural components are engineered as per IS standards (IS 15917 for mixed/composite prefabricated construction; IS 1893 for seismic design), with leading manufacturers such as EPACK Prefab holding ISO 9001:2015 certification. The market spans a wide spectrum from basic single-room portable cabins for construction site accommodation to multi-room complexes for industrial staff guest houses and resort/hospitality eco-cabins. Key material variants include MS frame, GI frame, FRP, and wooden structures, with insulation options of PUF (polyurethane foam), EPS, and rock wool sandwich panels. The hospitality/resort segment (glamping pods, eco-resort cabins, modular villas) is an emerging sub-segment but remains secondary to the dominant industrial/institutional accommodation use case. Units are relocatable and reusable, a key differentiator from permanent construction. No mandatory BIS product certification applies specifically to prefabricated guest houses as a finished product — structural steel components follow IS standards for steel and the National Building Code.
